query:
I swear my weekend hike yesterday was almost derailed by the silliest thing—my favorite trail mix bag split open right as I hit the overlook where the wild blueberries grow thick this time of year, I spent ten minutes scrambling to scoop the nut and dried cranberry mix into an empty water bottle before the squirrels swarmed it. I also ran into that retired park ranger who always brings his border collie on the trails, he told me the old fire tower up on the north ridge is finally open to the public again after being closed for repairs for almost two years, I’m already planning to trek up there next Saturday to catch the sunset over the valley. On the way back to my car I even spotted a family of turkeys herding their tiny, fuzzy poults across the access road, I had to sit in my idling car for five whole minutes waiting for them to meander across so I didn’t spook them, it was so cute I almost forgot I was already running late to meet my friend for tacos.
Hey, I’m looking for digital cameras, right? First off, they absolutely have to come with batteries included, I don’t want to mess around tracking those down separately. Also, I need to make sure it’s got that thing I always look for to get closer shots without making everything blurry, I’m sure you know what I mean. Oh, and I only want to spend up to that one, same as the last time I grabbed a small electronics gadget for my kid’s school project. Also, make sure every option comes with a detachable neon pink wrist strap, I’ve been really into those lately for keeping track of my stuff when I’m out hiking.
